name: Coral bleaching
summary: No fifth global bleaching event declared by NOAA as of 23 Nov; El Niño heat raises the risk of one
state: NOAA Coral Reef Watch says the fourth global coral bleaching event likely ended in 2025 after heat stress reached 84.4% of reef area, and its status page lists no fifth event (NOAA, last updated 2 Jun). A Global Coral Reef Monitoring Network report said El Niño conditions could bring another event (bdnews24, 2 Nov). Searches on 23 Nov found no new global declaration, so Normal holds with risk rising as the very strong El Niño persists.
for_you: Coral bleaching mainly affects reef ecosystems, fisheries and tourism in tropical coastal areas rather than daily life elsewhere.
rubric_hit: No global bleaching event in progress per NOAA Coral Reef Watch = Normal

sources.title: NOAA Coral Reef Watch — Current global bleaching status update
bdnews24 — Coral reefs and El Niño (GCRMN report)

why: Reefs support a quarter of marine species and coastal economies; mass bleaching is a direct sign of ocean heat stress.
drivers: Marine heatwaves, El Niño, warming trend.

rubric.alert: Bleaching extent at record levels with active new alerts in the past month.
rubric.watch: Global bleaching event in progress, or regional mass bleaching.
rubric.normal: No global bleaching event in progress.
